newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon E-Systems wins $18.5 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon E-Systems wins $18.5 mln contract.

text.p: A Raytheon Co subsidiary said Wednesday it won a U.S. Army contract worth at least $18.5 million to develop, produce and install a radio frequency surveillance system at the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico.

Raytheon E-Systems, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Lexington, Mass.-based high technology company, won the competitive contract to build the system for the Army's Simulation Training and Instrumentation Command (STRICOM). The contract could be worth as much as $50 million if fully executed, the company said.

The system is designed to ensure that the missile base is free of radio frequency interference that could compromise base personnel's efforts to track and control missiles, drones and other vehicles during testing, the company said.
Raytheon said it will deliver two control centers and five testing sites during the 29-month, initial phase of the contract. It will also provide communications upgrades.
